# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The incumbent uses 16 LUTs and 34 FFs, with routed WNS 0.445 ns and WHS 0.208 ns, so timing is feasible. The objective is strictly fewer LUTs while retaining timing closure and every verification gate. The CRC update is an eight-step combinational loop; the design also has separate frame-state and output CRC registers. The current top requires `// @latency 1`.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the serial CRC loop with a factored parallel XOR network may reduce LUT usage below 16 while keeping the 34-register state and timing feasible.

## Instruction for generator
Replace `crc16_update`’s eight-iteration shift-and-conditional-polynomial loop with explicitly derived CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE output equations, factoring shared XOR subexpressions across output bits. Keep the existing frame-state update, output slot registers, ready/valid logic, reset priority, and top interface and latency annotation unchanged. Preserve the 16-bit result for all state and byte values, and retain the specified frame restart, stalls, simultaneous retire-and-accept behavior, and registered outputs.
